chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
“There is no harm in performing salat (prayer) between the graves, so long as he does not take the grave as a qiblah.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: And it has been narrated that there is no harm in performing salat (prayer) toward a qiblah in which there is the grave of an Imam. And the fundamental basis is what we have presented before.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship under discussion
key_terms.الْأَصْلُ: the foundational ruling or primary basis adopted by the author
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave, which must not be taken as a qiblah
key_terms.الْمَقَابِرِ: graveyards or graves, the location mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.قَبْرُ إِمَامٍ: the grave of an Imam, mentioned in the additional report
key_terms.قِبْلَةً: a direction of prayer, here meaning an object directly faced in worship

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) between graves or facing a grave in Shi'a hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that performing salat (prayer) among graves is permissible as long as the grave is not taken as a qiblah. It also mentions a report concerning praying toward a direction in which the grave of an Imam is present, while affirming that the primary ruling is the one previously stated.
